name: Kremlin transcripts
watch: Near-full transcripts of Putin's talks, press conferences and joint statements with Xi and US envoys.
cav: Russian framing. Compare with the Chinese and US readouts of the same meeting.

name: China MFA readouts & daily briefings
watch: Leader-call readouts, daily press transcripts and policy papers such as the Global AI Governance Initiative.
cav: The wording changes in small steps over time. Look for phrases that are added or dropped.

name: Russian MFA
watch: Statements on arms control, strategic stability and talks with Washington and Beijing.
cav: Some pages are geo-blocked outside Russia.

name: US State Dept & White House readouts
watch: US readouts of calls and summits, with fact sheets after major meetings.
cav: US framing. Readouts are often shorter than the Kremlin's.

name: UN Digital Library voting records
watch: Recorded votes of all three on the same texts, including resolutions on AI in the military domain, disarmament and Ukraine.
cav: Votes are binding acts. How a country votes says more than its speeches.

name: UN Treaty Collection
watch: Who signed and ratified what, including reservations and withdrawals.
cav: Slow to update for bilateral deals.

name: China treaty database
watch: Full texts of China's bilateral agreements, including with Russia.
cav: Chinese-language search works best.

name: Russia official legal portal
watch: Decrees and ratifications, such as the national AI strategy and the law suspending New START.
cav: The authoritative text of Russian law. May block foreign IP addresses.

name: Federal Register
watch: Export-control rules, tariff actions and Entity List additions, published as binding text.
cav: The legal text is often more precise than the press release.

name: Congressional Research Service
watch: Nonpartisan briefs on arms control, sanctions and China–Russia ties, with citations.
cav: Written for Congress from a US-interest point of view, but careful with facts.

name: US-China Economic & Security Review Commission
watch: Hearing transcripts with expert testimony and a long annual report.
cav: Its mandate is adversarial. Use it for the sources it cites, not its conclusions.

name: China Customs statistics platform
watch: China–Russia trade by HS code: chips, machine tools, vehicles, oil. Russia stopped publishing detailed data in 2022.
cav: The best single window into China–Russia trade. Check it against UN Comtrade mirror data.

name: US Census trade with China
watch: The monthly US–China goods balance. USA Trade Online gives HS-code detail.
cav: Records the country of origin, so goods rerouted through Vietnam or Mexico look non-Chinese.

name: UN Comtrade
watch: Mirror statistics: compare what A says it exported with what B says it imported.
cav: Gaps reveal transshipment through Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Türkiye and the UAE.

name: IMF trade & COFER reserves
watch: Direction of trade and currency composition of reserves. Measures de-dollarization in actual numbers.
cav: COFER does not identify individual countries' reserves.

name: IMF PortWatch
watch: Port calls and chokepoint transits built from satellite ship tracking. A near-live view of trade.
cav: Ships that switch off their transponders (the shadow fleet) are undercounted.

name: USDA FAS GATS
watch: Soybean, grain and meat sales to China. A quick test of whether trade-truce purchase pledges are being kept.
cav: Weekly export-sales reports move faster than customs data.

name: CREA Russia fossil tracker
pub: Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (Finland)
watch: Russian oil, gas and coal exports by buyer and by ship.
cav: Open method, but the group campaigns for sanctions.

name: Bank of Russia statistics
watch: Balance of payments and currency structure of settlements, such as the yuan's share.
cav: Many series have been coarsened since 2022.

name: SAFE (China FX regulator)
pub: PRC State Administration of Foreign Exchange
watch: China's balance of payments, reserves and cross-border yuan flows.
cav: Reserves held in US Treasuries are partly hidden through custodians.

name: US Treasury TIC data
watch: Chinese holdings of US Treasuries.
cav: Holdings in Belgium and Luxembourg custody accounts can mask Chinese ownership.

name: SWIFT RMB Tracker
watch: The yuan's share of global payments.
cav: Excludes China's CIPS system and Russia's SPFS, which carry much of China–Russia settlement.

name: BIS international banking statistics
watch: Cross-border bank claims between the three countries.
cav: Lags by about two quarters.

name: WTO disputes & tariff profiles
watch: Formal complaints between the US and China, and the panel rulings.
cav: The Appellate Body has been paralysed since 2019, so rulings often go nowhere.

name: USTR Section 301 actions
pub: Office of the US Trade Representative
watch: Tariff lists, exclusions and the deal texts behind truce announcements.
cav: Check the Federal Register for the binding version.

name: MOFCOM export controls & Unreliable Entity List
watch: Rare earth, gallium and germanium controls, and US firms placed on blacklists. These are China's countermoves, written as law.
cav: Announcements often appear in Chinese first.

name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries
watch: How dependent the US is on Chinese and Russian rare earths, gallium, titanium and uranium.
cav: Annual, so it lags fast-moving export-control fights.

name: EIA Uranium Marketing Annual Report
watch: Russia's share of US enrichment purchases as the 2024 import ban phases in, with waivers possible through 2027.
cav: A quiet example of US–Russia trade that continues despite the conflict.

name: Rosstat
watch: Domestic output, inflation and industrial production, which show how much strain the war economy is under.
cav: Many series were suspended or reclassified after 2022.

name: OFAC sanctions lists (SDN)
watch: Chinese and third-country firms designated for supplying Russia. The press releases name specific items and routes.
cav: A US view of the facts, but each designation carries specific evidence.

name: BIS Entity List & chip rules
pub: US Commerce Dept, Bureau of Industry and Security
watch: AI chip and chipmaking equipment controls. Entity List additions of Chinese firms tied to Russia's military.
cav: Each rule includes a long preamble explaining Washington's reasoning.

name: EU Sanctions Map
watch: EU sanctions packages that name Chinese and Hong Kong entities supplying Russia.
cav: A third-party government source that is useful for checking US designations.

name: DOJ export-control prosecutions
watch: Sworn indictments describing China-to-Russia evasion networks and GPU smuggling.
cav: Allegations until proven, but rich in detail.

name: CourtListener (court dockets)
watch: Full filings behind the DOJ press releases, including exhibits and plea agreements.
cav: US courts only.

name: CAC algorithm & generative-AI filings
watch: Registry of approved Chinese AI models and services. Shows how fast China's model ecosystem is growing.
cav: Chinese-language. Lists approvals but not capability.

name: NIST CAISI & US AI policy
watch: US government evaluations of frontier models, including Chinese ones, and AI Action Plan follow-through.
cav: Its mission is framed around US competitiveness.

name: UN CCW talks on autonomous weapons (GGE LAWS)
watch: Each state's written positions on lethal autonomous weapons, side by side in one forum.
cav: Consensus rules mean slow progress, but the statements are on record.

name: UN AI governance (Scientific Panel & Global Dialogue)
pub: UN Office for Digital & Emerging Technologies
watch: The one AI governance forum where all three take part, created by the General Assembly in 2025.
cav: Early stage. Watch who sends senior delegations.

name: Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of AI
watch: The list of endorsing states shows who has joined the US-led norms on military AI.
cav: China and Russia have not endorsed it. The absence is itself the signal.

name: OpenAlex (research co-authorship)
watch: Raw counts of US–China and China–Russia co-authored papers, a measure of cooperation that persists through politics.
cav: Free API. Count the papers yourself instead of relying on anyone's chart.

name: CSET Emerging Technology Observatory
watch: Open datasets on AI research, patents, chips and investment.
cav: A US think tank with security framing, but the data is downloadable.

name: Epoch AI datasets
watch: Training compute and model releases by country, and the size of the compute gap.
cav: Coverage of Chinese labs depends on what they disclose.

name: Stanford AI Index
watch: The annual cross-country benchmark for AI talent, investment, papers and policy.
cav: A secondary compilation. Follow its citations back to the raw data.

name: WIPO PATENTSCOPE
watch: Patent filings by applicant country in AI, semiconductors and batteries.
cav: Patent counts measure volume, not quality.

name: Brookings–Tsinghua AI dialogue
watch: Unofficial (Track 2) agreements on military AI risk and nuclear command, written by people close to both governments.
cav: Not official policy, but often an early sign of where the official channels go next.

name: CTBTO monitoring network
watch: The global network of seismic, radionuclide and infrasound sensors. All three countries host stations and share data.
cav: The detailed data goes to member states. The public sees statements after events.

name: EarthScope / IRIS seismic data
watch: Raw waveforms from stations near Lop Nur, Novaya Zemlya and Nevada, the test sites at the centre of resumed-testing claims.
cav: Anyone can check it independently. Telling small tests apart from earthquakes takes expertise.

name: IAEA PRIS reactor database
watch: Every power reactor, including the Rosatom-built units at Tianwan and Xudapu in China.
cav: Covers civil reactors only.

name: IAEA statements & Zaporizhzhia updates
watch: Reports from inspectors on site at Zaporizhzhia, plus board statements where all three speak.
cav: Board diplomacy is political, but the inspectors' reports are first-hand observation.

name: State Dept arms control compliance report
watch: US findings on Russian and Chinese adherence to arms control and testing commitments.
cav: One-sided. Compare Russian MFA rebuttals.

name: New START data archive
watch: The last verified warhead and launcher counts. The baseline for any informal limits after the treaty expired on 5 Feb 2026.
cav: No more on-site inspections. Watch whether either side publishes counts at all.

name: NPT Review Conference 2026 documents
watch: National reports and working papers of the three nuclear powers. Compare with P5 joint statements.
cav: Final documents often fail by consensus. The working papers are the substance.

name: Missile launch notification agreements
pub: US State Dept / PRC & Russian MFAs
watch: US–Russia (1988, run through each side's Nuclear Risk Reduction Center) and China–Russia (2009, extended 2021) advance notices of launches.
cav: Some of the last working nuclear hotlines. Watch for mention of a missed notification.

name: FAS Nuclear Notebook
watch: Warhead estimates built from satellite imagery, budgets and official data, such as China's silo fields.
cav: Estimates, not counts. The method is explained.

name: SIPRI Yearbook (nuclear forces)
watch: The annual inventory of the world's nuclear forces.
cav: Swedish government-funded. Broadly regarded as even-handed.

name: Japan Joint Staff press releases
watch: Maps, flight tracks and photos of joint China–Russia bomber flights and naval transits.
cav: A third country's radar data, published with photos. One of the best open sources.

name: Taiwan MND daily PLA activity
watch: Daily counts of PLA aircraft and ships with track maps.
cav: Taiwan is a party to the dispute, but the counts are consistent and verifiable over time.

name: ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff
watch: Notices of Chinese and Russian aircraft entering South Korea's air defense zone (KADIZ).
cav: Mostly Korean-language.

name: NORAD news
watch: Intercepts in the Alaska air defense zone, including joint China–Russia bomber flights.
cav: Gives few details beyond the intercept itself.

name: US Coast Guard news (Arctic)
watch: Sightings of Chinese and Russian vessels in the Bering Sea and Arctic, including joint coast guard patrols.
cav: Event-driven, with no regular cadence.

name: DoD releases & China Military Power Report
watch: The annual estimate of PLA forces, plus readouts of US–China military talks.
cav: A US threat assessment. Compare it with Chinese defense ministry rebuttals.

name: China MND press conferences
watch: Announcements of joint exercises with Russia and readouts of talks with the US military.
cav: Read for what is announced and what is denied.

name: Russian Ministry of Defence
watch: Exercise announcements, including joint drills with China. Its Telegram channel is often faster.
cav: Often blocks foreign visitors. A party to the war in Ukraine.

name: Space-Track.org
pub: US Space Force (18th Space Defense Squadron)
watch: The official public satellite catalog: proximity operations, debris events and new launches.
cav: Free registration. Classified objects are left out.

name: CelesTrak
watch: Orbital data and analysis tools, independent of any government.
cav: Partly built on Space-Track data.

name: Jonathan McDowell's space catalogs
watch: A meticulous independent launch and satellite log.
cav: Run by one person, but widely cited by agencies.

name: UN Register of Objects Launched into Space
pub: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs
watch: What each state formally declares it launched. Compare against tracking data.
cav: Declarations are late or incomplete. The gaps are the signal.

name: SIPRI arms transfers & military spending
watch: Russian arms exports to China and military spending of all three in comparable dollars.
cav: Spending figures use estimates for China and Russia.

name: UN Register of Conventional Arms
watch: Self-reported arms imports and exports.
cav: Reporting is voluntary and patchy. Compare against SIPRI.

name: ACLED conflict events
watch: Coded events from the war in Ukraine.
cav: Built from media reports. Western-funded.

name: NASA FIRMS fire detection
watch: Heat signatures from refinery strikes, depot fires and industrial activity.
cav: Fires are not always attacks. Confirm with imagery.

name: Conflict Armament Research (iTrace)
watch: Field documentation of components found in Russian weapons: which country made them and the supply chains.
cav: Physical teardown evidence. Partly funded by EU governments.

name: ADS-B Exchange
watch: Unfiltered aircraft transponder data, including some military, VIP and tanker flights.
cav: Many military aircraft fly with transponders off.

name: Copernicus Browser (Sentinel-1/2)
watch: Free optical and radar imagery of ports, bases, test sites and borders. Radar sees through cloud.
cav: 10 m resolution shows ships and construction, not aircraft types.

name: USGS EarthExplorer (Landsat)
watch: A free imagery archive going back decades, for before-and-after comparisons.
cav: Coarser than Sentinel-2 for recent imagery.

name: NASA Worldview (VIIRS night lights)
watch: Night lights show industrial activity, blackouts and new infrastructure.
cav: Daily but coarse. Best for trends.

name: Global Fishing Watch
watch: Ship tracking and detection of dark vessels from radar and transponders, including tankers serving Russia's shadow fleet to China.
cav: Founded with Google and Oceana. Data is open and methods are published.

name: International Space Station
watch: US–Russia integrated crews and seat swaps continue despite the war.
cav: The clearest sign of US–Russia cooperation. Watch the planning for retiring the station.

name: ITER fusion project
watch: All three countries are members and deliver hardware to one reactor.
cav: Progress reports show whether each member is delivering its components on time.

name: Antarctic Treaty Secretariat
watch: All three are consultative parties. Inspection reports cover each other's bases.
cav: Decisions need consensus. Watch for proposals that get blocked.

name: North Pacific Fisheries Commission
watch: A fisheries body where all three still set catch limits together.
cav: Low politics, so cooperation here holds up.

name: WMO weather data exchange
watch: The global system through which national weather services share observations. It has kept working through every crisis.
cav: Watch for any member cutting data sharing.

name: Cospas-Sarsat search & rescue
watch: A satellite rescue-beacon system founded by the US and the Soviet Union. China runs ground stations in it.
cav: Cold War cooperation that is still running.

name: Nature Index collaboration tables
watch: Research collaboration scores between each pair of countries.
cav: Covers selected journals only. Use OpenAlex for raw counts.

name: IIE Open Doors
watch: Chinese student numbers in the US, a slow-moving measure of people-to-people ties.
cav: Lags visa policy by about a year.

name: Pew Research Center
watch: How people in many countries view the US, China and Russia, with comparable questions across countries.
cav: Cannot poll freely inside China.

name: Levada Center
watch: Russian views of the US and China, tracked over decades.
cav: Russia has labelled it a "foreign agent". Wartime answers may be less candid.

name: Tsinghua CISS public opinion surveys
watch: Chinese public views of the US and of international security.
cav: Conducted inside China's political limits, but a rare data point.

name: Chicago Council surveys
watch: American views of China and Russia, tracked since 1974.
cav: US public only.

name: Xinhua / People's Daily
watch: The official line. Shifts in adjectives about the US or Russia mark changes in policy.
cav: Read for intent, never for fact.

name: TASS
watch: The Kremlin's narrative, and often the first report of Russian statements.
cav: Read for intent, never for fact.
